messages.author: d4c7167e7e0c951f
messages.subject: dplyr - close db connections?
parts:
Between all the dplyr::backend_db() functions, I've completely eliminated the need to require( RMySQL/RPostgreSQL), except for closing a connection/src, for which I must still use RMySQL::dbDisconnect(src$con).

Because I am very prone to connections expiring quickly, I need to open/close connections on every single query.

So is there a way to do this inside dplyr?

Also, I would love to use temporary/cached tables per shiny user session, but because I use new connections on each query I can't.  Is there a workaround, or do I just need to create/delete a permanent table per session (or figure out why my connections expire so quickly!)?

Thanks.

messages.author: d4c7167e7e0c951f
messages.subject: Re: dplyr - close db connections?
parts:
I guess I don't know the reason, I always figured it was some sort of systems-imposed constraint like, 'if no activity within 1 minute, close connection', or 'periodically drop connections not coming from prod servers'.  It's interesting/telling to me that this is raising a flag with you.  Losing connections is such a common break in code that I don't even go 2 queries without open/closing, or using tryCatch.  But now I want to utilize cached tables in dplyr. 

So maybe I need to figure out this question before proceeding.  Is that why there is no dplyr::db_disconnect?  I've always read that it's rude to not close unused connections, so I was confused that I can open a connection within dplyr but not close it.

FWIW, It's always this error message (I don't believe it actually always loses connection DURING the query, but before): 

"Error in mysqlExecStatement(conn, statement, ...) : 

  RS-DBI driver: (could not run statement: Lost connection to MySQL server during query)

"

messages.author: 8502567f9dbc7c7e
messages.subject: Re: dplyr - close db connections?
parts: One possible issue might be if you are automatically starting a relational transaction upon opening the connection then keeping that transaction active without a commit would be, ah, impolite, and a DBA might configure the connection to drop if left open. This could be configured at the database end or possibly the client end. IMO having this configuration would be bad form at either end, but there are different strokes for different folks so it could be affecting you.

parts:
Thanks for the info, I don't think that is it though.  Might have been an InfoBright issue, which we're no longer using.  Or, because I query production requests from me somehow have less priority or more propensity to be dropped.  Or just connection issues - I am the only one who really queries actively from my location so that could explain why I get dropped and not production queries.

It's funny that I wasn't aware that this was something I should be concerned about.  Didn't realize the extent that I was just hacking.  But I'm really glad that the conversation went in this direction so that I know it's an issue, can take care of it, and can hopefully get the temporary table caching working.

By the way, I will be attempting to make Vertica a src db.  Has anyone tried this?  Should it be expected to work given Vertica's distributed nature?  I will update in a few weeks after I've attempted it.

On Friday, November 21, 2014 2:06:13 PM UTC-8, jdne...@gmail.com wrote:
One possible issue might be if you are automatically starting a relational transaction upon opening the connection then keeping that transaction active without a commit would be, ah, impolite, and a DBA might configure the connection to drop if left open. This could be configured at the database end or possibly the client end. IMO having this configuration would be bad form at either end, but there are different strokes for different folks so it could be affecting you.

On Friday, November 7, 2014 6:33:39 AM UTC-8, Hadley Wickham wrote:
Yes, I'd strongly recommend that you figure out why you're losing the
connections before you attempt any other work arounds.

Hadley
